We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts: 168.60, 143.85, 130.30, 22.80, 21.35, 19.20 ppm.

We need number of CH3 groups (methyl). In 13C NMR, methyl carbons appear around 10-30 ppm (aliphatic). Here we have three signals in that region: 22.80, 21.35, 19.20. Likely three distinct methyl carbons. Could any be other types like CH2? CH2 also around 20-40 maybe. But typical CH2 (methylene) around 20-40 as well. Need to determine if they are methyl groups. Additional info: we have carbonyl at 168.60 (likely carbonyl C=O), aromatic/sp2 at 143.85, 130.30. So the molecule likely has aromatic ring with carbonyl (maybe acetophenone derivative) and three methyl groups attached perhaps to aromatic ring (like toluene substituents) or aliphatic chain.

But we need count of CH3 groups. The presence of three distinct aliphatic carbon signals suggests three methyl groups, unless some are CH2. Could we get proton NMR to confirm? Let's retrieve proton NMR for the sample? We don't have SMILES. Could use proton_nmr_spectra tool but need SMILES. Not available. Could use HSQC to correlate but need sample. Could request HSQC.
